newsitem.title: INDIA: India to set up oil refinery in Orissa - minister.
newsitem.headline: India to set up oil refinery in Orissa - minister.

text.p: India's junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu was quoted on Saturday as saying an oil refinery costing an estimated 85 billion rupees ($2.4 billion) would to be set up in the eastern state of Orissa.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Balu as saying the proposed refinery would be commissioned near the port town of Paradip during the ninth five-year plan period beginning on April 1, 1997.
The news agency quoted Balu as saying the refinery would be set up by the state-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) in a joint venture with the Kuwait Oil Corp.
Both IOC and Kuwait Oil Corp will hold an equity of 26 percent. The rest would be raised through market borrowing, Balu said.
Balu was speaking at a news conference in Orissa's state capital Bhubaneshwar.
He said the the annual capacity of the refinery will be increased to nine million tonnes from six million planned earlier.
"The change in capacity has been approved by the IOC board last week and I will get it approved in the cabinet soon," PTI quoted Balu as saying.
He said an investment of 106.31 billion rupees has been envisaged for the devlopment of Orissa's oil sector during the ninth plan.

Apart from the refinery, the other projects that would be taken up in Orissa include three petroleum storage tanks and a 390 km pipeline from Paradip in Orissa to Ranchi in the neighbouring Bihar state.
A liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) import facility at Paradip and two LPG bottling plants would be set up during the ninth plan, Balu added. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
